_doc: THE THINKER CATALOG -- data, not code. organs/thinker.py is the ONE reader; it refuses a catalog whose entry lacks
a field Round 0 measured (model-choice unit, round0/facts.json, schema mc_r0_facts_v1, 2026-09-26). One adapter per
transport (cli, http-ollama, http-openai); a backend is an entry here, never a branch in an organ.
Placeholders resolved by the seam at call time, never here: {call_home} (a fresh per-call scratch HOME, deleted after),
{thinker_home} (<VOIDLOOM_ENV_DIR or ~/.voidloom>/thinker, mode 0700), {model}, {prompt}.
binary.names are searched on PATH and binary.candidates (~ = the caller's HOME) at PROBE time; the ABSOLUTE path found
is what `voidloom thinker set` records, because kimi is not on the timers' PATH (facts: kimi.on_timer_PATH false).
POSTURE BY PURPOSE (owner, 2026-09-26: the minimum tools each organ needs now, widened only by a deliberate, recorded
act). `text` serves the seven synthesis organs; `research` serves gap research alone. A backend with web=false has no
research posture: gap research on it is a LOGGED SKIP, never invented research (the 0.5B invented it in Round 0).
Every variadic claude flag (--tools, --allowedTools, --disallowedTools) sits BEFORE a single-valued flag (#21971):
placed last, it swallows the prompt and `claude -p` exits 1.
THE a-f QUESTION, word for word (KAEL-EM's wording; the owner's rulings of 2026-09-26: e) Not now approved, and the
question is asked on every interactive install and upgrade, before anything is laid; 2026-10-16: d) Gemini added,
e) Not now KEEPS its letter and words, Other moves to f), and the documented non-interactive answer is the backend
NAME, never a letter). install.sh asks it (THE ASK HELPER), install/install_crons.sh names it when it refuses to arm
a brain with no recorded answer, and README.md + docs/ONBOARDING_GUIDE.md quote it for an installing AI agent --
voidloom/tests/test_installer_questions.py binds all four to these strings as FIXED TEXT. options: [letter, the words
shown, the answer `voidloom thinker set` (and install.sh --thinker) takes]. letter_notes: printed once when a letter
whose meaning changed on 2026-10-16 is passed as a flag (one release; scripts pass names). program_words: how the
installer names a backend's program when it offers the vendor's installer (`get` is the command). signin_screens: shown
before a backend's own sign-in (`voidloom thinker login`) starts -- {program}, {thinker_home}, {model} filled in.
question.ask: Should your brain think while you sleep, and with which model?
options: Gemini (Google; runs through Google's Antigravity program)
Not now — no model; keep the simple nightly routines
question.chat_note: The model you chat with can be a different one: this answer is only about the thinking your brain does on its own, overnight.
question.agent_rule: If you are an AI agent running this installer for someone: stop, put this question to them word for word, and pass their answer as --thinker claude|codex|kimi|gemini|off|local -- never choose it yourself.

letter_notes.d: note: --thinker d now means d) Gemini. Until 2026-10-16 d) was Other (a model on this computer): for that, pass --thinker local. Scripts should pass the name, not the letter.
letter_notes.f: note: --thinker f now means f) Other (a model on this computer; it was d) until 2026-10-16). Scripts should pass the name: --thinker local.

claude.adds: one program to ~/.local/bin (claude), its versions in ~/.local/share/claude, a download folder ~/.claude/downloads, and possibly a PATH line in your shell's startup file

codex.adds: one program to npm's global folder (codex, ~/.npm-global when that folder is in your home), and npm's own cache ~/.npm

kimi.adds: one program to ~/.kimi-code/bin (kimi), its install folder ~/.kimi-code, and possibly a PATH line in your shell's startup file

gemini.adds: one program to ~/.local/bin (agy), a staging folder ~/.cache/antigravity, its own settings folder ~/.gemini, and possibly a PATH line in your shell's startup file

gemini: Found Antigravity at {program}. The brain gets its OWN Google sign-in, in {thinker_home}/gemini-home.
Your everyday Gemini sign-in is not touched. Uses your plan's quota; no bill.
Overnight model: {model}. Google may use these conversations to improve its products.
Antigravity asks a few setup questions first (theme, trust); any answer is fine.
Then open the link it shows in your normal browser, sign in, and paste Google's code back here.

history._doc: agy's own per-conversation stores in the brain's home (r1 reflection F1): each entry older than keep_days is pruned under the gemini lock before a call starts, at most once per every_hours; index rows of removed conversation files are deleted, but agy restores them from jetbox_summaries_proto.pb on its next call (measured 2026-10-16: 29 orphan rows back, ~460 B raw_summary each): full transcripts are pruned, per-conversation summaries (~1 KB a call) are kept. The sign-in file is never a candidate. prune is ON: MEASURED 2026-10-16 -- a populated home (574 entries / 30.0 MB, 29 conversations) pruned to 112 entries (151 removed, 29 index rows, the sign-in kept), then ONE real call through the brain's sign-in in the sandbox passed (19.9 s, gemini-3.8-flash; it added 19 entries / 0.89 MB) (iterations/r1_fix_handoff.md).

_doc: One line per operating system (Python's sys.platform, with linux* read as linux): 'supported', or the
refusal the owner reads. The darwin line is the ONE place the owner's Mac ruling flips (the macOS Keychain
is per user, not per folder, so a sign-in of the brain's own is unproven there).
platforms.darwin: Gemini is not yet available on Mac: the Antigravity program keeps its Google sign-in in the macOS Keychain, which belongs to your user account rather than to a folder, so the brain cannot have a sign-in of its own there without sharing yours. That is the owner's ruling for now (2026-10-16); choose another option on a Mac.
